h1: Engineering intelligent systems. Building new possibilities.
sub: I research a problem, make its assumptions and constraints explicit, then build and test a practical implementation. My work spans programming languages and compilers, systems architecture, symbolic cognitive computing, agent platforms, and backend products. I value explicit specifications, deterministic behavior, controlled authority, and evidence that a system works—not merely a design that sounds complete.
w_l: Selected work across programming languages, symbolic computing, agent platforms, research, and full-stack products. Project maturity is stated plainly.
c_l: Implementation-focused studies from selected projects that have executable code or active development. Maturity and unresolved qualification are stated plainly.
c_1: The normative Edition 1 grammar is the source of truth. Implementation behavior must not be invented when the specification is silent or inconsistent.
c_2: The roadmap separates a minimal Rust core, a broader Rust platform, and a future independently qualified self-hosted compiler. The later stages are targets, not completed milestones.
c_3: Keep grammar, semantics, implementation, tests, and qualification evidence aligned as the language evolves.

a_l: A disciplined, evidence-first approach: understand the system, make constraints explicit, implement in controlled steps, and verify the result before calling it complete.
a_1: Inspect the live repository, specifications, architecture, history, and runtime evidence first. Separate verified facts from assumptions, and identify the actual root cause before editing.
a_2: Turn goals into explicit requirements, invariants, ownership, permissions, interfaces, and acceptance criteria. Resolve contradictions rather than hiding them behind implementation shortcuts.
a_3: Prefer root-cause fixes over cosmetic patches. Keep changes scoped, preserve history, avoid unrelated rewrites, and make each milestone independently reviewable.

p_helios: Concept and specification for a cognitive-computing architecture with an entirely non-neural symbolic core: deterministic rules, explicit knowledge, managed memory, symbolic reasoning, planning, and controlled actions. Frozen foundation models are quarantined perception-only peripherals; their outputs are provenance-bearing, untrusted observations—not facts or authority. No runtime exists yet.
detail_omni: The latest inspected main-head checkpoint is 27c55651d8d20c4d46d1fb28a3c440770b9d4363 (9 November 2026). The Rust, Clippy, security-audit, and CodeQL workflows passed, while the aggregate Omni CI pipeline and a fuzz-dependency workflow failed. The repository still classifies the compiler as early-stage; formal foundation sign-off, complete-language conformance, production readiness, and self-hosting remain unresolved. Individual passing gates do not qualify the compiler as a whole.
detail_helios: Helios is currently architecture and specification research. Its intended trusted core is entirely non-neural and symbolic: deterministic logic, explicit knowledge structures, managed memory, symbolic reasoning, planning, and action authorization. Frozen foundation models are isolated perception peripherals only; their outputs carry provenance as untrusted observations and must never be treated as facts, beliefs, or authority. No runtime implementation exists. Specification conflict to resolve: the current Helios README still prohibits all pretrained models and inference services, so the newer perception-only exception has not yet been reconciled in that repository's canonical specification.
detail_aether: The repository describes a specification and host-reference prototype, not an operating-system kernel. The QEMU RISC-V64 product slice has not started.
detail_mosaic: The repository labels the current line a candidate and explicitly reports full-release qualification as blocked. A substantial implementation is not the same as a qualified release.
detail_nexus: The repository identifies version 0.3.0-alpha.5 as an unreleased prerelease. It should be presented as an evolving alpha, not a stable product.
detail_kilo: This is your local fork of upstream Kilo Code. Those capabilities must be attributed to your experimental fork only, not to upstream Kilo Code; the public repository needs fork-specific evidence and documentation before they can be presented as published functionality.

a_4: Run type checks, unit and integration tests, browser tests, builds, and relevant security or deployment checks. Exercise failure paths and regressions—not only the happy path.
a_5: Keep documentation and the issue ledger current. Report exactly what changed, what passed, what remains blocked, and what still needs an owner decision. Never equate an agent's success message with proof.
case_omni_intro: Omni is an early-stage Rust compiler and toolchain governed by a normative Edition 1 language specification. Current work includes compiler foundations and executable ownership/region prototypes; complete-language conformance and self-hosting are not claimed.
case_omni_1: The Edition 1 grammar and linked specifications define the language contract. Compiler behavior is not invented where the specification is silent or contradictory; grammar, semantics, implementation and conformance cases evolve together.
case_omni_2: The Rust workspace contains lexer/parser foundations, type and name-analysis work, ownership-state and MIR foundations, plus isolated research prototypes for region and memory behavior. Research prototypes provide evidence but are not automatically production compiler components.
case_omni_3: Focused Rust, Clippy, security and CodeQL checks have passed on inspected revisions, while aggregate pipeline and fuzz-dependency gates have also failed. Full-language conformance, formal foundation sign-off, production readiness and self-hosting remain open.
case_helios_intro: A research architecture for a trusted non-neural symbolic core with frozen perception-only models.
case_helios_1: Reasoning, memory, planning, policy, and action authorization remain deterministic and symbolic.
case_helios_2: Frozen models may produce candidate observations with provenance; outputs are never facts, beliefs, instructions, or authority.
case_helios_3: The public Helios README still conflicts with the newer perception-only exception and must be reconciled before implementation claims.
case_nexus_intro: NexusAgent is an unreleased 0.3.0-alpha.5 local-first agent platform with executable single-agent and team modes. Its repository describes real AgentLoop workers, specialist roles, shared team coordination, dependency-aware execution, memory, MCP, RAG, tools and provider routing.
case_nexus_1: The single-agent path runs an agent loop with workspace, shell, Git, web and MCP tools. Agent profiles can be built-in, global, user, project or workspace scoped, with explicit scope precedence.
case_nexus_2: Team mode creates actual AgentLoop workers rather than simulated placeholders. Workers receive bounded roles, share a persistent team blackboard, exchange messages and operate across dependency-aware stages.
case_nexus_3: The 0.3.0-alpha.5 version is an unreleased prerelease. Hosted providers, local models, tool permissions and team recovery need continued end-to-end qualification before a stable API or production claim.
case_uep_intro: UEP is an actively developed 0.15.0.0-SNAPSHOT education and training operations platform. Its Java/Spring Boot and React source spans tenant-aware identity, academic administration, scheduling, attendance, announcements, learning resources, assessment, grading, academic review and live-class workflows.
case_uep_1: Organization membership, branch scope and role-based access are represented across the platform. PostgreSQL tenant-aware relationships and self-scoped learner/teacher APIs are designed to prevent one workspace or persona from crossing another's boundary.
case_uep_2: The source includes academic structures, enrollment, teaching assignments, timetable occurrences, attendance, announcements, notification outbox, learning-content uploads, assessments, grading and academic-review services, plus role-aware web workspaces.
case_uep_3: The repository is still a snapshot. Local Windows acceptance, external identity/database services, complete persona isolation and production deployment evidence must pass before calling the platform production-ready.
case_kilo_intro: A personal Kilo Code fork with checked-in experimental work on staged swarm execution. The fork history includes a change that fails an incomplete stage instead of silently accepting a missing handoff. NVIDIA NIM routing and broader orchestration remain experimental and must not be attributed to upstream Kilo Code.
case_kilo_1: The public README still describes upstream Kilo Code. Fork-specific functionality must be documented and reviewed separately; upstream editor, CLI and provider capabilities are not evidence that this fork's experimental swarm is complete.
case_kilo_2: The fork's staged execution work treats a missing handoff as a failed stage rather than silently reporting completion. Architect, implementer, tester and reviewer responsibilities need explicit inputs, outputs and acceptance conditions.
case_kilo_3: NVIDIA NIM and specialist-agent routing are development targets, not a claim of a released or fully qualified swarm product. Keep local experiments, checked-in code and upstream features distinguishable.

case_mosaic_intro: Mosaic is a substantial tokenizer and token-processing runtime candidate built around exact source-byte preservation. Its native C runtime, Rust workspace and Python binding cover deterministic tokenization, Unicode-aware projections, streaming and incremental processing; full cross-platform release qualification remains blocked.
case_mosaic_1: The implementation keeps original bytes intact, provides byte-fallback representability, maps tokens to exact source spans and executes deterministic, validated model packs. Higher-level Unicode and language views do not replace the original source.
case_mosaic_2: The repository contains online streaming, incremental TokenDocument updates, Unicode segmentation and security analysis, normalization provenance, a native C ABI, and Python wrappers over the native runtime.
case_mosaic_3: The project has extensive native, Rust and Python test infrastructure, but its latest recorded full qualification still had failing or unavailable fuzz, Miri and platform gates. It remains a candidate, not a stable release.
case_dnc_name: Dynamic Neural Computation — executable reference platform
case_dnc_intro: DNC is an implemented Python research/reference platform for structured dynamic-computation graphs. It includes graph validation, planning, scheduling, runtime state, checkpoints, replay, provenance and provider interfaces; full tensor-native execution and external production qualification remain open.
case_dnc_1: Graphs are validated as directed acyclic graphs. Module preconditions, dependency order and ownership constraints govern what can execute; the planner constructs and validates a runnable execution graph.
case_dnc_2h: State that can be inspected and replayed
case_dnc_2: The reference runtime includes working memory, append-only history, checkpoints, restore/rollback, execution traces and provenance-oriented observability so state changes and failures can be examined.
case_dnc_3: Repository records describe a governed reference platform. The latest recorded cross-platform gate had a Python 3.11 floating-point assertion failure, and the Phase 16 pilot readiness decision was NO-GO pending independent canary evidence.
case_tensor_intro: A Python/PyTorch library implementing tensor-ring factorization for large embedding tables. The repository includes configurable rank and compression targets, ALS/SVD initialization, pretrained conversion and quantization/export paths; release readiness and reproducible quality claims remain unverified.
case_tensor_1: TensorRingEmbedding represents a large embedding table using tensor-ring factors. Configuration can be expressed through rank, target parameter count or target compression, making the memory/quality trade-off explicit.
case_tensor_2: The code covers ALS/SVD and related initialization, pretrained embedding conversion, serialization, optional Hugging Face integration, and quantization/export tooling such as GGUF-related paths.
case_tensor_3: Parameter-count reduction alone does not prove faster inference or equivalent model quality. The repository's latest status report flags test-workflow startup and security-gate failures; reproducible benchmarks and clean CI are required before a release claim.
